sections.sectionSummaryBrief: These three aspects also apply to the teshuvah of returning the sparks to their source.

translations.translation: Now, these three matters mentioned above also apply to the teshuvah of returning the sparks
(that are in physical things)
to their source,
for in this teshuvah as well there is a parallel to the three matters above.
First,
the thirst and longing of the sparks
(from the perspective of their root)
to ascend from their descent and return to their source,
like the lower waters that weep, saying, "We desire to be before the King."
Second,
the great joy that results from the elevation of the sparks and their return to their source after having been distanced.
And third,
since the sparks that fell into the shells,
even into the shell of Nogah,
had their light extinguished,
therefore, from the perspective of their state, it is not possible for them to be refined and elevated to their root,
and when they are refined and ascend to their root
(through the service of man),
it is a novelty.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The novelty in the teshuvah of returning sparks is greater than the novelty in simple teshuvah.

translations.translation: And it can be said
that the novelty in the teshuvah of returning the sparks is a greater novelty than the novelty in simple teshuvah.
For in simple teshuvah,
even though before teshuvah he was in a state where he did not do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, as above,
this is only as it is in externality,
but his true will
(even then)
was to fulfill the will of his Creator
(as per the well-known ruling),
except that this will was in a state of extreme concealment,
to the extent that its revelation is like a novelty.
However, this is not the case with the teshuvah of returning the sparks to their source,
for since the sparks that fell into the shells
(even into the shell of Nogah)
had their light darkened,
to the point that they are not in the category of light at all,
their refinement and elevation is a true novelty.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The advantage of thirst from distance is primarily in the teshuvah of the soul, while the joy from closeness of sparks is like that of two friends.

translations.translation: However,
this matter
(the superiority in the teshuvah of returning the sparks)
is in the quality of the novelty in teshuvah.
But the quality of the thirst that comes from distance is primarily in the teshuvah of the soul
(both in the teshuvah of the righteous and in simple teshuvah).
For since the connection of souls with G-dliness is an intrinsic connection,
like the connection of a son with his father
("You are children to the L-rd your G-d")
which is an intrinsic connection,
therefore, when the soul feels that it is distant from G-dliness
(the distance caused by its descent below,
and certainly the distance caused by sins),
this touches its very essence,
and consequently,
the thirst caused by the feeling of distance also touches its essence.
And so too regarding the delight from the closeness that comes after the distance,
for since souls are children,
for a son is from the very essence of the father,
the delight of the father from his son drawing near
(after having been distanced),
and all the more so his only son,
is an essential delight.
However, the delight from the closeness of the sparks after they have been distanced is like that of two friends
who have not seen each other for a long time, and when they draw near and see each other,
they delight and rejoice greatly,
a delight which,
(though it is a great delight),
is like other delights that come from something external to oneself.
